title: Gamma rack ops bullet clipboard
content:
Context: quick personal scratchpad for Gamma rack (row G, pods 7-10) — morning checks and items to hit before handoff. Mostly shorthand. Keep this updated if anything is changed during shift.

MORNING PRIORITIES (top of mind)
- Goal: leave cluster at >= 78% pool availability for hosted-api (gamma-pool) before 10:30 PT. Today target = 6 spare GPUs.
- Watch thermal pattern on node-g7-09 — saw two nvlink timeout warnings overnight; temp peak ~86C. Might need limit change or reflow on airflow.

QUICK CHECKS (order):
[ ] 1) ssh ops@gamma-g7-09 -> sudo journalctl -u kmsvc -f (look for nvlink/backpressure)
[ ] 2) kubectl get pods -n inference --selector=pool=gamma-pool -o wide | grep Evicted
[ ] 3) check free GPU count: ./scripts/gpu-pool-status.sh gamma | awk '{print $2" free"}'
[ ] 4) network paths: ping 10.42.7.1 (top-of-rack) & traceroute to rgw-01.redwood.internal

NOTES / OBSERVATIONS (raw)
- 03:14 AM spike: 2x preemptions on gamma-pool - suspected autoscaler oscillation after a failed launch. See OPS-874 for launch failure trace.
- Node g7-09 reported PCIe reset at 02:48; kernel dmesg shows "AER: Corrected error" repeated. Might be flaky riser.
- I kicked a rolling restart for exporter sidecar on noisy pod (hash: ae3f7). Reduced token-level CPU from 76% to ~42%.

ACTION ITEMS (this shift)
- Try soft drain + restart on g7-09 if nvlink warnings repeat:
  - kubectl cordon node/g7-09
  - drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
  - reboot -> monitor dmesg for repeats
- If repeated PCIe AER errors after reboot, tag hardware: tag node g7-09 "hw:possible-riser" and file hardware ticket with rack diagram.
- Add a small guard in node-autoscaler config: minimal-stabilization = 60s to prevent oscillation. Test in staging.

NETWORK / STORAGE QUICKIES
- Ephemeral disk pressure shows on /var/lib/kubelet on g7-10 (85% usage). Temporary cleanup: docker image prune + kubelet rotate logs. Run: sudo du -sh /var/lib/docker/* | sort -h to find large dirs.
- NIC reset command (if packet drops >0.3%): sudo ethtool -r eno3 && sudo systemctl restart network-monitor.service

TEMP SCRIPTS / ONE-LINERS
- free-gpus: python tools/pool_free.py --pool gamma --min-free 6
- recent kernel logs for node: ssh ops@g7-09 "sudo journalctl -k --since '2 hours ago' | tail -n 100"
- quick memory pressure check for pods: kubectl top pods -n inference --containers | sort -k3 -n | tail -n 12

TICKETS / FOLLOW-UPS
- OPS-874 (launch flaps) -> follow up with release-eng for AMI config used in gamma. (assigned Marcos)
- HW-412 (possible riser replacement) -> file if g7-09 shows repeated AER after reboot.
- PR #1294 (autoscaler stabilization) -> link above; need to run canary on staging gamma-pool.

HANDOFF NOTES (to next shift)
- If g7-09 reboots OK, mark "rebooted-2026-03-10" in node annotations and add short note in OPS-874 comment.
- If free GPUs dip below 4 and autoscaler hasn't reacted in 90s, escalate to oncall SRE (pager: /ops/sre-oncall).

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs (personal)
- Is there a long-term plan to move gamma-pool to the new NVLink topology? Who owns that roadmap? (cc: infra-arch)
- Confirm whether kernel 5.15 backport fixed AER noisy logs — check internal cherrypicks in PR history.

RANDOM SCRATCHES
- coffee: buy a replacement fan for rack G (Fan model: delta-0915) — talk to facilities.
- reminder: update the "gamma-pool capacity cheat sheet" in Confluence with todays' observed baseline (avg free = 5.8 GPUs)

END-OF-SHIFT QUICK CHECKLIST (before leaving)
- [ ] mark handoff in Slack #gamma-ops with short bullet list + OPS-874 link
- [ ] commit any quick fixes to infra-playbooks/gamma (small patch) and reference PR
- [ ] confirm room temp under 25C in rack (sensor G7-RTemp)

Misc shorthand:
- wip: reduce gpu-job timeout from 90m -> 60m for experiments queue (helps reclaim) -- test locally first
- note: exporter bump to 1.8.2 fixed noisy metrics, but may increase scrape CPU by ~3% per pod

---
Timestamp: 2026-03-10 09:12 PT
Saved local copy -> will paste into drive if any major updates.
